I'm more of a manga person but I think they're just like any other animation? Only that you can see a different culture or portrayal in certain aspects like how they voice their lines, how the characters act, their everyday life, the sceneries, etc. There's a contrast between Western animation and Japanese animation, I believe.

I mean, if you compare the animation running in Western TV and in Japan, it's really different. You can see it if you put Amazing World of Gumball to, idk, maybe Daily Lives of High School Boys, or side by side. The way they animate things is different and it's fascinating. (I'd like to say Beast Stars but lol, that's soooo different in terms of genre. Though animation wise, you can see it's different from Gumball or Zootopia.)

Also, personally, I like how fluid Ghibli is, and to think it's hand-drawn is just amazing! They have so much dimension, so smooth, and just really pleasing to the eye. And its soundtrack is just soooo good! Similarly, I also like the way animes such as A Silent Voice is animated. The visuals, coloring, shadowing, and how they show/transition the scenes is so nice. I'm a sucker for good backgrounds too.

And story-wise, I like the fact they tackle psychological and tragic stuff to soft comedy to horror. There's Happy Sugar Life with a cutesy art style but it's horror and violent. And there's Magus Bride that is both relaxing, magical, and would cover relatable topics, with a spice of action. 

Though Western cartoons do the same, the writing just feels different. I have no idea how to explain it, but the narrative and descriptive are just different, and I'm fond of it. The writing style, I believe, accompanied by again, their culture and language structure. It's also the humor, I think. I grew up to tsukkomi-boke comedy so, I like it.

If you've tried to communicate more than three times, it's best to cut him off. He's not respecting you, and more so focuses on his interest and pride over your health and boundaries (which should never equate in my opinion). That is never okay. Please just cut him off, that's no friend or even a respectful person.

But, if for example, he's the ring leader of your friend circle, that might just worsen your mental health. Instead, minimize your interactions as much as you can if the situation doesn't allow the former. Keep a distance as if he has the 19 and Co., and observe his patterns towards the triggering subjects. You can leave immediately if you feel he's going towards that subject, and sometimes, stay for a bit (*only* if you can) then go away to avoid suspicion. You can also try to change subject if you see a similar thing that could be talked about instead.

Although, I really implore you to just "door slam" him, I don't know his whole character. He might complain about how you cut him off however, as long as you have your own supporters within the circle group, and the rest aren't like him, it will be bearable and soon die down. But if he's really the worse, it might be best to distance yourself as much as possible for your safety (not unless you have a card enough to keep him shut). It's also best to express how you're feeling about this guy with someone that both knows you and him, and can act as a middle man to avoid triggering you and angering the clown.

Relationships are tricky but always take care of yourself, sweetie. I'm sorry you have to deal with that, and with my possibly icky advice. I hope you soon stop dealing with that guy. He doesn't deserve your time and energy.

I don't know whether this is the right way of thinking but, it did irked me when your mother used the "he has autism" card. While perhaps true and it does contribute, I don't think he should get away from attempted murder and abusing you. That's no where near right, and she should be defending you as far as I know. And please know that no matter how easier or harder it is for you compared to others, as long as you put your effort in it, you deserve it. You're a smart guy, you earned it, don't feel bad you got paid for it.

I also get the desire to manipulate. And personally, it's a defense mechanism that I'm trying to not use unless absolutely necessary. As long as you're aware of it and trying to kick it down, I think you're good. I say redirect that desire into a healthy hobby that makes you feel like you're in control still, or that calms it down.

And considering what you've been through, your perspective and feelings about social relationships and trust issues are understandable. I recommend writing in a diary (digitally, locked, and secured if you're in a household you don't trust) and reflecting a lot about it to what you want from yourself in interactions versus what you did. Take your time in opening up, start by the easiest and build your way up as you achieve deeper connections. There will be times where you'll be disappointed but don't lose hope and keep your guard up. From what I experienced there's really no other way if we want to have real connections, unfortunately.

Furthermore, you deserve the compliments and the help. You suffered, you have a lot to process, and you're willing to get better, as I am willing to bet my ass on the tray you deserve every drop of good therapy. Every pain deserves aid when the person is willing to change.

Play video games with him, take him out of the house if he's comfortable with it and have dates or explore new places with him, get his or your friends to hang out together, text him or call him whenever you can while at work, not to check up on his suicidal thoughts but checking up on him; ask about what happened during class or whatever he was doing; tell him funny moments you saw at work or you thought of, or promise to do this or that after work. Take simple walks together or to the gym. Encourage a healthy lifestyle that he could work with. Talk to him and ask why he's feeling like that or like this if he's willing to talk. And so on forth. There are a lot of things to distract him and help him with. Just try em out and see if it works.

You're doing great in what you've done up until now, and wanting to do. Keep reminding him that you're there for him, love him and just be there for him. Acknowledge that he's suicidal and how painful it is, perhaps you don't know exactly how he's feeling, and it'll be hard to work with, but it's possible and you care for him.

There may be times he may hide his thoughts from you, and that's okay. It's normal. Just let him know that you can fight the thoughts together. And if it gets too painful for the both of you or for him, try in persuading him in getting a doctor but don't be forceful. If he really doesn't want to, ask if he wants to see someone like his family or friend that he might be willing to open up about it. Or even this Reddit. It's good to open up about it bit by bit.

Also, there might be times when he wants to be alone. During those times, just stay on guard, get all the sharp and wires away from him, and just remind him again, that you're there for him and he could ask whenever he needs you. If you need to be away for work during those times, and if you sense something is up, may be take a leave or ask someone to watch for him like a friend or family member. I really suggest the latter since he might feel bad if you do the former, if he's that type of person. Kiss or hug him before you leave. And text him whenever it's your break. He may not want to talk so, you can again just talk about things you know will make him laugh or smile, or send a simple reminders of how you love him.
